scope: Proof of EXACTLY route obligation R3 of the rank-deficient route, in both the pointwise and the locally uniform version. With R1 and R2 that is three of the route's thirteen numbered items. R0, R4-R10, N1 and N2 remain OPEN and the rank-deficient part of the codimension-m coarea critical set remains OPEN. NO coarea formula, NO slicing statement and NO Sard theorem is proved. No hole migrated. No existing .lean file modified, aggregate import untouched. The log-concave Cheeger-Buser line belongs to collaborator Wang Haocheng and was not touched.

why_R3_is_needed: the route slices inside a fibre of the regular component, and a chord of a fibre is NOT a tangent vector: two points of one fibre give only a small bound on the regular component's differential applied to the chord, not zero. Turning that into smallness of the full differential needs the quantitative statement that a vector almost annihilated by a surjection is close to its kernel, which is a norm bound on a right inverse.
why_the_uniform_version_is_a_hard_requir: the epsilon to zero limit of the Eilenberg argument runs through a DIFFERENT approximating partition at every scale, so a constant depending on the piece is useless; the bound has to hold with one constant on a whole neighbourhood

main_results.core_estimate: exists_mem_ker_norm_sub_le: a right inverse R of L makes z - R (L z) killed by L and within ||R|| ||L z|| of z; NO surjectivity, NO finite dimension, NO completeness is used
main_results.pointwise: exists_rightInverse_bound: a surjection onto a finite-dimensional space admits a single constant C putting every vector within C ||L z|| of the kernel; the continuous right inverse comes from Mathlib's HasRightInverse.of_surjective_of_finiteDimensional
main_results.perturbation: rightInverse_comp_inverse: if A composed with R0 is a unit of the operator ring then R0 composed with its inverse is a right inverse of A
main_results.uniform: exists_nhds_uniform_rightInverse_bound: around a point where the differential of a C1 map is surjective there is a neighbourhood carrying ONE bound M on the differential and ONE constant C for the kernel estimate, proved by perturbing a single right inverse at the base point via Units.isOpen and NormedRing.inverse_continuousAt, giving C = 2 times the norm of that right inverse

stronger_than_the_route_asked.coareaJacobian_translation: the route's coareaJacobian (fderiv v x0) != 0 is converted to surjectivity by the proved coareaJacobian_ne_zero_iff, so inner products enter only in that translation

what_surjectivity_is_and_is_not_needed_f.it_makes_the_right_inverse_exist: no_right_inverse: the rank-one projection of the plane admits no right inverse, so the construction used to prove R3 is unavailable for it
what_surjectivity_is_and_is_not_needed_f.it_is_NOT_forced_by_the_pointwise_conclu: pointwise_conclusion_does_not_imply_surjective: the zero map satisfies the pointwise conclusion with C = 0 while failing to be surjective, so THIS ROUND DOES NOT CLAIM SURJECTIVITY IS NECESSARY for the pointwise half
what_surjectivity_is_and_is_not_needed_f.not_proved: the (true) statement that in finite dimensions EVERY linear map satisfies the pointwise conclusion is NOT proved here
what_surjectivity_is_and_is_not_needed_f.the_uniform_hypothesis_does_real_work: uniform_constant_degenerates: along t times the identity the smallest admissible constant is the reciprocal of |t|, which blows up as the family approaches the non-surjective zero map, so no neighbourhood of such a point carries a single constant

boundary_cases.zero_dimensional_target: every map surjective, C = 0 works and every vector is already in the kernel
boundary_cases.linear_isomorphism: the inverse is the right inverse
boundary_cases.constant_map: the differential vanishes identically; the uniform statement is available exactly when the target is zero-dimensional and is then trivial

not_done: R0, the rank-deficient part, is untouched
R4, the tangential small-Lipschitz estimate, is NOT proved and is the POINT OF NO RETURN: with R2 and R3 in place it is self-contained, and if it fails the route is wrong
R5 through R10, N1 and N2 are unproved
no coarea formula is proved and the applicability of the proved codimension-m coarea formula is unchanged
no Sard theorem: nothing is claimed about the measure of the set of critical values
